minutes.headline: Assessors line-edited their formal response to the select board's investigation report; no votes except adjournment
minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors spent nearly the entire meeting doing a line-by-line edit of the department's written response to the select board's investigation report, covering the board vacancy, cyclical inspection wording, income/expense data, second-home and chapter land directives, and open positions; Sarah Cameron agreed to draft an addendum arguing the investigation left key issues unaddressed. The board also signed off on a senior real estate tax exemption brochure for printing, set a run of future meeting dates through December, and decided no executive session was needed for the next meeting.

budget_items.what_was_said: The board edited wording so that any personal property valued below the town's exemption threshold is exempt from personal property tax; the threshold itself was not disputed, only the sentence describing it.

The board agreed to have the two-part brochure combined into one document and printed on glossy paper by an outside printer, ordering no more than a stated quantity of copies unless more are needed; cost was not stated.

decisions.decision: Add a line to the investigation-response document noting the vacancy on the Board of Assessors.
State in the report that filling the vacant assessor seat should be a priority, and highlight that sentence when presenting to the select board.

Sarah Cameron will draft an addendum arguing the investigation report did not fully address communication/oversight issues or offer remedies; to be reviewed at the next meeting and appended to the document.
No changes needed to the senior real estate tax exemption brochure; combine the two files into one document and send to a printer on glossy paper.
If no venue is available for the 24th, check the Adult Activities Center or fall back to the 25th (a Thursday).
Tentatively set October 1st and October 15th (first and third Wednesdays) as the next two regular meeting dates.
Tentatively set November 5th and 19th, and December 3rd and 17th as meeting dates.
Reach out to the Appellate Tax Board before the next meeting to find out if there are any outstanding cases against Lunenburg.
The assessor's office will pull its own sales report from the deeds before receiving Vision's analysis.
No executive session is needed for the September 13th meeting since there are no pending exemption or chapter land matters.

what_happened.line: The Board of Assessors spent most of the meeting line-editing its written response to the select board's investigation report.
Sarah Cameron agreed to draft an addendum arguing the investigation left oversight and communication issues unaddressed.
The board decided to flag its own vacant seat as a priority to highlight when the response goes to the select board.
The senior real estate tax exemption brochure was approved without content changes, to be combined and sent to a printer.
Meeting dates were tentatively set into December, and no executive session is planned for the September 13 meeting.

why_it_matters: The response document is the assessors' formal answer to a select board investigation into the office, and its wording will shape how that oversight review is resolved.
The tax exemption brochure supports the senior real estate tax exemption program, which lowers property tax bills for qualifying seniors who apply.
No budget figures were voted on; the only budget-adjacent item was a wording clarification about the personal property tax exemption threshold, not a change to it.
